new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both listed works were marked silent; I spot-checked both (whole text read and a full-text search for stress/accent/prosody terms in both). Neither says anything about word stress or accent placement. Jenkins & Amdahl's only prosodic sentence is the p. 6 tone-ignored line already quoted; the decree's 'accent' is only the acute/circumflex diacritic name and its Art. 6 'forte'/'faible' central vowels are a vowel-quality contrast, not stress. Nothing missed.

tone_statements.citation: Merrill, John T. M. 2018. The Historical Origin of Consonant Mutation in the Atlantic Languages. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley. Appendix sec. 2.1.2 'Bedik', pp. 284-286 (data from Ferry 1968a, 1991).
tone_statements.quote: Ferry identifies three level tones for Bedik, and no contour tones. The tones of Bedik are generally flipped from those of Bassari and Konyagi, so that where the other languages have a high tone, Bedik has a low tone, and vice versa. … In this latter work, the tones given on the prefixes in the Bedik data are not consistent with those laid out in the table in the introduction, where certain prefixes are listed with no tone, others with a mid tone, and other with a high tone.
tone_statements.locator: Chapter 5 'The Tenda languages', sec. 2.1.2 'Bedik', p. 286; cf. sec. 2.3.1 p. 296 on prefix tones and sec. 3.1.1 p. 314

tone_statements.quote: Le mënik est également une langue à tons et à classes nominales, développant aussi des harmonies vocaliques et des alternances consonantiques la base du radical des noms, des adjectifs et des verbes.
tone_statements.translation: Mënik is also a tone language and a noun-class language, which further develops vowel harmonies and consonant alternations [at] the base of the root of nouns, adjectives and verbs.
tone_statements.locator: p. 1 (Résumé); English abstract p. 2 repeats it ('Mënik is also a tone and nominal classes language')

sources.note: A morphosyntactic article (reciprocal suffix -ər, reflexive -aya, valency) whose résumé gives a one-sentence typological profile stating explicitly that mënik is a tone language with noun classes, vowel harmony and consonant alternation. No tone inventory, no tone rules, and the mënik examples throughout are written in the untoned practical orthography (ə ɓ ɗ ŋ ʃ ɲ; no tone diacritics). It is nevertheless the first open, first-hand text listed here that states Bedik/Ménik is tonal (consistent with Ferry's three-level tone marking and Sorosoro's 'classes tonales').
